heading: Worlds to walk through
intro: Interactive reconstructions built from the collections I work with: you can walk through a corpus, a century or a statistical argument.

entries.title: Roodkapje
entries.subtitle: The Forest of Tellings
entries.blurb: Walk the forest as Little Red Riding Hood. Every fork in the path is a variant attested in 427 Dutch tellings, from 1781 to 2015, and the real words of those books keep you company along the way.
entries.alt: Little Red Riding Hood, her grandmother and the rest of the cast in a forest clearing at dusk, among drifting golden motes.

entries.title: Nachtdienst
entries.subtitle: Night duty in the Centraal Sagenarchief, 1983
entries.blurb: Twelve envelopes to file before midnight. Four card cabinets, and a room that is itself the lock: the clock, the window, the door, the typewriter. Every puzzle is built from the 9,659 stories of the Dutch Folktale Database.
entries.alt: The reading room of the Centraal Sagenarchief by lamplight, with card cabinets, a long-case clock and the window onto the canal.

entries.title: Op ’t Water
entries.subtitle: Amsterdam’s song-book trade, 1600–1700
entries.blurb: Every song book in the Dutch Song Database that names an Amsterdam printer, placed at the address in its imprint on Gerrit de Broen’s engraved map. Then step down onto the quay where the trade was busiest.
entries.alt: Gerrit de Broen’s engraved map of Amsterdam, with red and blue song books stacked on the printers’ shops.

entries.title: Diversity under collection bias
entries.subtitle: A companion to the Royal Society Interface paper
entries.blurb: Set up two assemblages, bias how their records were collected, and see which standardization strategy still recovers the true diversity ratio.
entries.alt: Richness curves for two assemblages by sample size and by coverage, from the interactive demo.
